title: Annotatio V §.XI open: Quinta Probatio — Ignoratio Elenchi; Irenaeus duabus rebus in confessions
pass_a_gloss: XI. The Fifth and last Proof of the most distinguished Professor had ended where the first began, namely in Ignoratio Elenchi — opposing to the Reformed, who attack Oral Eating of Christ’s body, Irenaeus’s words teaching that the Holy Supper consists of two things, heavenly and earthly, inserted in the Reformed Sendomirian, Torunian, and other Confessions, as such as the Reformed embrace with both arms.
pass_b_english: §.XI: the Professor’s fifth and last proof ends where the first began — Ignoratio Elenchi.
He sets Irenaeus’s “two things, heavenly and earthly” (in Sendomir, Toruń, and other Reformed confessions the Reformed gladly embrace) against those who deny Oral eating of Christ’s body.
source_text: XI. Quinta postremaque Clarissimi Professoris Probatio, in eo desierat, in quo prima cœperat, nempe, in Ignoratione Elenchi, opponendô Reformatis, Oralem corporis Christi Manducationem impugnantibus, Irenæi verba, quibus S. Cœnam ex duabus rebus, cœlesti & terrena, constare docetur, Reformatorum Confessionibus Sendomiriensi, Toruniensi aliísque inserta, tanquam talia, quæ ambabus ulnis amplectuntur Reformati.

lemmas.gloss: of two things, heavenly and earthly
